title: skill-feedback-issue: reports cannot say whether the fix or only the symptom was verified (GH#8)
description: The body template puts 'Where it comes from' (a line number, cheap to confirm by reading) directly next to 'Proposed fix' (not confirmable by reading at all), with no field distinguishing what was actually established. Step 1 says 'confirm each claim at a line number', which covers the symptom only. A reader takes 're-verified against the installed source' as covering the whole report. Reported consequence: three of five issues filed by this skill against godot-selftest-harness carried a proposed fix that would not have fixed the bug, each caught only because the implementer reproduced the mechanism before applying the diff.
acceptance_criteria: A Verified field with an honest default, a step 1 sentence separating symptom-confirmation from fix-correctness, and an evidence-bar clause that a checkable fix gets checked. Composes with the Environment line's spotted-by rather than duplicating it.

title: skill-feedback-issue: installPath is not necessarily the directory the skill ran from (GH#7 item 1)
description: Step 1 resolves installPath from installed_plugins.json and says to re-verify there. The cache keeps every version ever installed side by side - eight for this plugin right now - and the directory a skill loads from is not guaranteed to be the one installed_plugins.json records. This is the one skill whose entire premise is that a stale install produces false alarms, so a line number confirmed in a tree that did not execute is that exact failure arriving through the front door. Verified: 0.6.0 vs 0.10.0 differ by a whole skill plus eight templates.
acceptance_criteria: The reconciliation is mechanical, not a paragraph the reader may skip, and it answers whether the skill's own files differ between the two versions.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#7 as resolve_skill.py plus the step 1 rewrite; 8/8 behaviour cases pass including the reported 0.6.0-vs-0.10.0 scenario.

title: juice_test.gd always exits 0, even when it fails
description:
Found by tools/verify_skill.py and independently confirmed. skills/godot-game-ui-juicy/assets/juice_test.gd ends its check sequence by printing 'JUICE: ALL PASS' or 'JUICE: N FAILED' and then 'return true' from _process — returning true from a SceneTree's _process quits the tree with exit code 0 REGARDLESS of the result. Its sibling smoke_test.gd does this correctly: quit(0) on pass, quit(1) on fail (smoke_test.gd:127-132).

So any loop that judges juice_test.gd on its exit code has never seen it fail, and CLAUDE.md's own documented workflow ('run, read stderr, not just the exit code') is the only reason this has not bitten yet. verify_skill.py works around it by requiring the marker line as well as exit 0 and clean stderr, which is the right defence in the runner, but the script itself should still be honest.

Fix: mirror smoke_test.gd — quit(0) in the pass branch, quit(1) in the fail branch, before 'return true'. Not done in the same pass because another agent held skills/godot-game-ui-juicy/ at the time.

Verification: mutate a juice assertion's subject in a scaffolded copy, confirm 'echo $?' is 1 rather than 0, then restore and confirm 0.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/backlog-round-2: juice_test.gd now calls quit(0)/quit(1) before 'return true', mirroring smoke_test.gd:127-132. Proven against Godot 4.7.1 in a scaffolded probe: baseline raw exit 0 with JUICE: ALL PASS; with ui_juice.gd's motion-disabled path mutated to leave alpha at 0, JUICE: 1 FAILED and raw exit 1; restored, raw exit 0. Before the fix the mutated run also exited 0.

title: gh#10 follow-up: store art should photograph the title screen; cover replace-vs-remove
description:
Second comment on GitHub issue #10, same session, same skill.

1. Art recipe. store_art.py cover/banner --title (pixel-font composite over a gameplay shot) produced a banner the user rejected outright — the chunky pixel title fought a game whose art is smooth vector and whose title screen already renders its name in its own font. What worked: capture the TITLE SCREEN with the menu hidden (bridge set-state visible=false on buttons/labels, nudge the title labels, re-space scenery, screenshot) and integer-crop 960x400 / 630x500. The Art section should lead with 'if the game has a title screen, photograph it — composite text only when there is nothing to photograph', and store_art.py should get a --no-title mode (crop + optional scrim, no text) plus a note that the pixel-grid title is right for pixel-art games and wrong for vector ones.

2. Replace vs remove. On the edit form's cover widget, clicking the widget's .button while an image is set opens the picker and REPLACES the image — no removal needed. Clicking .remove_image_btn from JS froze CDP for 45s (a native confirm, most likely). On the theme editor's banner widget it is the other way round: with an image set the only control is 'Remove image', and Upload appears only after it (safe, no dialog). Both belong under 'Uploading images'.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/backlog-round-2. Art section now leads with 'photograph the title screen; composite only when there is nothing to photograph', framed as a trap because nothing errors — the only signal is a human calling it awful. Measured first: omitting --title ALREADY produced a text-free integer crop, so --no-title was added as an explicit guard (exits 1 if --title/--subtitle is also passed) rather than as new behaviour. The one real bug found: add_scrim sat inside the text branch, so '--scrim left' with no title wrote a byte-identical file — now honoured. Existing behaviour byte-proven unchanged (sha256 identical for cover --title, banner --title, banner bare). New 'Replacing an image that is already set' subsection covers cover-replaces-in-place vs banner-requires-remove, and why .remove_image_btn froze CDP for 45s.

title: Lint SKILL.md Markdown (log S-043)
description: SKILL.md is the product in this repo, so a rendering bug is a defect in the deliverable. A **bold** paragraph placed immediately after a list item with no blank line is absorbed into that bullet as a lazy continuation - introduced one this session and caught it only by reading the diff. Nothing lints Markdown here.
acceptance_criteria: Stdlib-only script in the palette_lint.py mould covering lazy continuations, unclosed fences and headings without a preceding blank line. Shown to FAIL on the bug that prompted it, and shown silent on all current SKILL.mds.
close_reason: Done on branch fix/backlog-round-2: tools/lint_markdown.py (stdlib-only, palette_lint mould). Covers lazy continuations, unclosed fences and headings with no blank line above. The lazy-continuation rule is narrow BY DESIGN — indentation cannot separate the bug from a wrapped bullet line (both at column 0), so it fires only on block-shaped leads CommonMark cannot start mid-paragraph (**strong**, table row, link reference definition). Wrapped prose and HTML comments are exempt by rule, not by allowlist, so no ignore pragma exists. Documented cost: a PLAIN prose paragraph glued to a bullet is not caught, being indistinguishable from wrapped text. Verified: silent on all 13 tracked .md (and 16 under skills/), fires on the original **bold**-glued-to-bullet shape; 37 lint cases in tools/smoke_test_tools.py, SMOKE: ALL PASS.

Adding a model to a kit' is 3D-only and hands the gate to blender-mcp-modelling style_probe.py --check, which has no 2D equivalent. title: itch-devlog: Body row has the same Redactor textarea-sync gap as itch-store-page
description:
Found while fixing gh#10. skills/itch-devlog/SKILL.md:145 documents the devlog Body as 'textarea[name="post[body]"]', edited through the .redactor-layer contenteditable — click into it and type'. It names the real posted field (better than the store-page row did) but never says to mirror the editor HTML into that textarea, so if synthetic typing fails there the way it did on the edit form, a devlog saves with an empty body.

Also: the devlog form's editor class is .redactor-layer while the store edit form returned .redactor-in on 2026-08-17. Either itch runs two Redactor versions or one observation is stale — which is itself the argument for the resolve-the-contenteditable guidance now in itch-store-page's SKILL.md, and itch-devlog should probably adopt it verbatim.

Not fixed with gh#10 because it is a different skill and the .redactor-layer vs .redactor-in question should be settled by measurement against a live devlog form, not by inference. A cross-reference to itch-store-page's blank-screenshot gotcha would also fit next to itch-devlog's existing 'serializing this page can wedge the renderer' warning.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/backlog-round-2. itch-devlog's Body row no longer says 'click into it and type' (that instruction is what produces an empty post); a new section carries the store page's defence — resolve the editor via .redactor-in -> .redactor-layer -> [contenteditable=true], mirror into textarea[name=post[body]], assert ta.value.length before Save. The prose states plainly that the store form returned .redactor-in while the devlog form was recorded as .redactor-layer, that nobody has checked a live devlog form since, and that this guidance is NOT verified against one — that unresolved disagreement is presented as the argument for the fallback chain. Cross-reference added between the renderer-wedging and blank-screenshot gotchas.

title: Add a throwaway-Godot-project probe script (log S-038)
description: Verifying a .gd template change means: write project.godot, scaffold, --import, copy the test, --script, and read stderr rather than the exit code. CLAUDE.md documents the steps but there is no script, and --import (whose omission causes a parse-error cascade in files nobody touched) is the easiest to skip. Hand-rolled four times in the GH#5 session alone.
acceptance_criteria: One script that takes a skill name and prints the pass/fail lines for every test that kit ships, palette_lint included.
notes: 2026-08-17: widen this. Two independent subagents fixing GH#9 and GH#11 both asked for the same missing thing — not just a Godot probe project, but a wrapper for CLAUDE.md's whole mutation-proof loop (copy check to scratchpad, patch the check out, run, read red, restore, re-run green). It was hand-rolled 4x in the itch-ci-deploy fix and 2x in the pause-menu fix, and it is the step most likely to be skipped under time pressure. The Godot-specific half is what this issue already describes (scaffold, minimal project.godot the scaffolder does NOT write, --import, smoke, juice, palette_lint, re-scaffold); the general half applies to any check in the repo, including the pure-Python smoke_test_scaffold.py.
close_reason: Done on branch fix/backlog-round-2: tools/verify_skill.py. Takes a skill name (or --all), discovers what it ships (scaffold_*.py, assets/*_test.gd, palette_lint.py, smoke_test_*.py), writes the minimal project.godot the scaffolders require but never create, and prints pass/fail for every lane. Verified green on godot-game-ui (5), godot-game-ui-juicy (6), godot-2d-placement-audit (3), itch-ci-deploy (1); clean explicit outcomes for a probe-only skill and an unknown name. --import is a TYPE not a step: run_godot_script takes an ImportedProject only godot_import can construct, and the import is verified by requiring every declared class_name back out of the class cache — the 'Could not find type GameHud' cascade is unreachable. Judges on marker line AND exit code AND stderr because none is sufficient alone. --mutate patches the scaffolded copy, requires red, restores, requires green (exit 0 = caught, 1 = the assertion is decorative). Two real findings: juice_test.gd always exits 0 (filed separately), and godot here is an extensionless sh shim that shutil.which cannot see.

title: godot-game-ui: the kit has no text-contrast guarantee across palettes
description: Measured while fixing the clinical button bug. At full opacity, secondary-button ink sits below WCAG AA 4.5:1 in five of six palettes (amber 4.00, bloodmoon 3.85, candy 2.78, noir 3.69, verdant 3.58) and bloodmoon's primary is 2.65 - a saturated blood red takes neither black nor white ink well. Not a regression: amber was ~4.0 before this change too, and buttons are translucent over gameplay so raw bg_color overstates it. But nothing measures contrast at all, so a hand-written palette can ship unreadable. Options: a contrast arm on palette_lint (needs the compositing assumption pinned down), or tuning the palettes.
acceptance_criteria: Either a measured guarantee, or a documented statement that the kit does not make one and what to check by hand.
close_reason: Done on branch fix/backlog-round-2. FIRST FINDING: the tracker's numbers were computed in the wrong colour space — they weight raw sRGB-encoded Color components as if already linear (Color.get_luminance()'s maths) against raw bg_color with alpha ignored. Under the real WCAG piecewise transform, composited down each pair's real layer stack, candy is 5.09 not 2.78, noir 6.66 not 3.69, verdant 6.67 not 3.58, amber 7.10 not 4.00. The compositing crux is settled by measurement: secondary buttons are 0.95 over a 0.88 panel over a 0.86 backdrop, so gameplay leakage is 0.084% — below one 8-bit step — and where leakage IS real (HUD pill, 32%) evaluating over both black and white bounds it with no assumption. ONE FIGURE HELD UP: bloodmoon's primary button was genuinely broken (4.14 normal / 3.47 hover, and neither black nor white ink could reach 4.5 against that red). Chose a hybrid: (a) a composited contrast arm on palette_lint with --contrast-table, 16 pairs, bars 4.5 and 3.0; ui_theme.gd's ink pick is now measured (best_ink/min_contrast/contrast_ratio/relative_luminance/composite exported for user screens) instead of a get_luminance() > 0.4 guess; (b) two palette values changed — bloodmoon ACCENT to (0.76,0.14,0.13), fixing primary hover 3.47 -> 4.79, and clinical TEXT_FAINT to (0.41,0.47,0.51), 3.00 -> 3.46, which the new check found unprompted; (c) documented honestly that the crosshair ring and bare Glyph draws have NO surface behind them so no ratio exists — the kit answers those with geometry, and the by-hand check is your brightest scene. Engine assertions added to smoke_test.gd reading real StyleBoxFlat.bg_color, because the lint replicates style_button's derivation and that replica is what goes stale. Verified: silent on all six palettes and both template sets, fires on the pre-fix bloodmoon accent (4.03) and on a hand-written unreadable palette (12 pairs), five engine assertions shown red against the defects they describe; SMOKE/JUICE/PALETTE green under all six palettes; five shared files still byte-identical.

title: File [G-007] upstream: godot-selftest-harness lint --find-orphans is opt-in
description: log.md 2026-08-15 commit pass on plant-tower-defense, harness 0.19.0. Committing WIP that added Plant.set_selected() with no caller: plain lint and the 43-test suite both passed; --find-orphans caught it immediately (WARN: res://game/plant.gd: set_selected() has no reference outside its own file). Nothing prompts the flag and /verify does not pass it, so the default gate is green on a feature that cannot run.
